info.title: Forte Advice Pinball
info.description: Scoreboards for the office pinball machines. Cabinets POST their whole high-score board; duplicates (same table + category + initials + value) are dropped. Scores are insert-only, stored as int64 and timestamped by the API, never by the cabinet. Categories are identified everywhere by their SLUG — the same identifier the cabinet memory maps use ("destroy_ring_champion"); labels are display only and never a key. Each machine has one main ranked leaderboard, slug "main", reported as category null, plus any number of achievement categories that may hold a score, a counter, a duration in whole milliseconds or an epoch timestamp.

get.summary: Health check (Foundry contract)
get.description: status is healthy, degraded or unhealthy. 200 for healthy/degraded, 503 for unhealthy. /healthz is kept as an alias that reports status "ok" for older probes.

get.summary: Foundry app manifest

200.description: Manifest — name, type, ui, api, capabilities, auth, health

get.summary: This document (also served at /openapi.json)
Scores for the CLI — category, initials, value
get.description: Plain text by default: one tab-separated line per score, columns category, initials, value. An EMPTY category column is the main ranked leaderboard (category null in JSON). Without ?table= the table id is prefixed as a first column. The main leaderboard comes first, then the achievement categories ranked by their own top value, alphabetical on a tie; values descend within a category. Split on TAB, not on whitespace, because of the empty column.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows kept per category (not per response). "slots" gives exactly as many rows as the cabinet keeps for each category (from its memory map) — what a writeback needs. "shown" uses each category's rows_shown, the same cut the website makes; "all" removes the cut.

category.description: The category SLUG, exactly as the cabinet memory maps spell it (lowercase, underscores). null is the machine's main ranked leaderboard — slug "main" — into which GRAND CHAMPION / HIGH SCORES / HONOR ROLL / … all collapse, rank derived from the score order. Empty first column in the text format.

slug.description: The same slug, never null: "main" for the ranked leaderboard.

label.description: Display name only — the machine's wording, admin-editable. Never use it as a key.

slots.description: How many places the cabinet itself keeps for this category, from its memory map.

ordering.description: "ranked" — position comes from the value. "positional" — the machine's slots are their own thing (Medieval Madness keeps four King of the Realm slots). Metadata; output is ranked by value either way.

value_type.description: How the bigint value should be read. score: the score itself. counter: how many. duration: whole MILLISECONDS (not seconds — cabinet fields such as the Lord of the Rings ring timer count hundredths of a second, and milliseconds keep those exact while the value stays an integer). timestamp: epoch seconds, UTC.

value_unit.description: Duration unit. On submission it is the unit of the value being sent (default ms) and is remembered as the category's native_unit; on output it is the unit the value is stored in — always "ms" for a duration, "s" for a timestamp, null otherwise.

native_unit.description: The unit the cabinet's own field counts in, when a submission or an admin has declared it (e.g. "cs" for a hundredths-of-a-second NVRAM timer). Divide the stored millisecond value by the unit to reproduce the exact integer the machine expects: 12340 ms / 10 = 1234 cs. Metadata only — it never changes how a submitted value is read.

value.description: int64 as a string, to keep full precision. Read it according to value_type: a score or counter as-is, a duration as whole milliseconds, a timestamp as epoch seconds.

score.description: Legacy name for value — same int64 string

display.description: The value formatted the way the website prints it, suffix included

metadata.description: Opaque per-row annotation the cabinet reads alongside the value, stored and returned VERBATIM as a string map. Medieval Madness' Kings of the Realm sends crowned_at (the coronation date the DMD shows — wall clock with no timezone, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"; it is never parsed, converted or given an offset) and crowned_count (how many times that player has been crowned, a decimal integer as a string). Never part of the dedup key: same table+category+initials+value is the same coronation whatever the metadata reads. Absent for every other category.

submitted_at.description: When the API first saw the score, not when it was achieved

post.summary: Submit a batch of scores (cabinet extractor)
post.description: Takes a whole board. Duplicates (same table + category + initials + value) are dropped, so most submissions are expected to be no-ops — that is the normal case, not an error. One bad row never fails the batch: every entry comes back in results with inserted / duplicate / echo / ignored / rejected and, when rejected or ignored, a reason. Unset slots need no filtering by the caller — initials holding no letter or digit ("   ", "---", "") are ignored, not rejected and not stored. Send a tables array of the boards this run READ (see the request body) to keep a board the server cleared cleared: rows that merely repeat what this source last showed come back as "echo" — not inserted, not entered into a running competition, not announced — while a genuinely re-earned score is still inserted. Echo is distinct from duplicate: duplicate means the server already holds this exact row; echo means the machine has not moved since its last report. Scores are insert-only and timestamped server-side; cabinet timestamps are ignored. Send X-API-Key if PINBALL_API_KEY is configured, and optionally X-Source to label the rows. X-Announce: off (or ?announce=false) stores the batch without announcing any of it in Slack, for a first sync, a backfill or a test fill; it applies to that request only and changes no setting. Provenance (map_version, extractor_version, source_slot) may be given per entry, per table, for the whole batch, or as the headers X-Map-Version / X-Extractor-Version. It is stored but never deduped on, so a corrected memory map does not re-insert the board; a row keeps the provenance of the run that first created it, and later runs reporting the same row are recorded as sightings.

map_version.description: Hash/version of the NVRAM memory map that produced the row. Never part of the dedup key: submitting the same board under a corrected map is still a batch of duplicates, not a new board.

extractor_version.description: Version of the CLI that submitted the row

source_slot.description: The physical slot the value was read from — rank is derived, so the slot is otherwise lost

tables.description: Every board the cabinet READ this run, including boards that held no scores — send it alongside scores. Listing a table turns on last-seen tracking for it: a board identical to what this source (X-Source) last reported contains nothing new, so its rows come back as "echo" rather than being re-inserted or announced, and a board listed here with no scores of its own is how the server learns a clear (competition start, a delete, a wipe) reached the machine — so an empty scores array is NOT a no-op when tables is present. A table that could not be read (missing/locked file, unmapped ROM) must be OMITTED, never listed empty: "read, empty" and "no information" must not be conflated. Omit tables entirely to keep the older behaviour (everything inserts, no last-seen state kept).

table.description: Overrides the batch table for this entry

category.description: The category slug from the memory map ("castle_champion"). null / absent / "main" / any main-board spelling => the main ranked leaderboard. A human label ("CASTLE CHAMPION") is still accepted and slugified to the same key, so an older extractor keeps landing on the same board.

label.description: Optional display wording for this category, straight from the map ("Castle Champion"). Stored as the category label; never part of any key.

slots.description: Optional: how many places the cabinet keeps for this category. Returned by ?limit=slots.

value.description: int64. Send anything above 2^53 as a string. With value_type "duration" the number is whole milliseconds unless value_unit says otherwise, and "12.34s" / "0:10:00" / "1:02.5" are also accepted; anything finer than a millisecond is rejected rather than rounded. With value_type "timestamp", epoch seconds or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM".

value_unit.description: Durations only: the unit of the value in this entry, default ms. Send the raw NVRAM integer with its own unit (1234 with value_unit "cs") and nothing is ever rounded. Remembered as the category's native_unit.

parameters.description: Rows kept per category. "slots" gives the cabinet's own slot count per category, "shown" follows the website setting, "all" removes the cut.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per category. Omitted means each category's own rows_shown — ten for a main leaderboard, three for an achievement category unless an admin changed it.

Initials mapped to office people
A table's playfield photo, downscaled
get.description: The machine picture rendered at (at most) the requested width and cached. Never enlarged: asking for a width above the original returns the original. Any other width is snapped to the nearest supported one (see /api/images/support). Public and permanent — Slack announcements point at this so the photo can be drawn smaller than full width.

302.description: The source image could not be rendered; redirected to it instead

404.description: Unknown table, or it has no picture

get.summary: Which picture widths this build can render
Competitions, running and finished
What the public claim form needs
get.description: Whether claiming is on, the allowed email domains, and every initials known — those seen on a board plus any already mapped to a person, each with its score count (0 for a pre-registered set).

post.summary: Claim initials as yours (no login, trust-based)
post.description: A visitor states which initials are theirs and gives a name and an allowed work email address. Unclaimed initials are mapped immediately (status approved); initials someone else already holds return status pending for an admin to resolve. Initials that hold no scores yet can be claimed too, so someone can pre-register before their first game — has_scores says which case it was. Scores are never modified.

confirm.description: Must be true — the claimer swears the scores are theirs

201.description: Claim recorded — status approved or pending

400.description: Missing field, unusable initials, disallowed email domain, or unconfirmed

429.description: Too many claims from one address

put.summary: Set a category label, value_type, display_suffix and rows_shown
put.description: The key in the path is the category slug; use "main" for the ranked leaderboard. Setting a label only changes what the website prints — it never moves a score.

value_type.description: How the bigint value should be read. score: the score itself. counter: how many. duration: whole MILLISECONDS (not seconds — cabinet fields such as the Lord of the Rings ring timer count hundredths of a second, and milliseconds keep those exact while the value stays an integer). timestamp: epoch seconds, UTC.

native_unit.description: Durations only: the unit of the cabinet field this category comes from

rows_shown.description: How many places of this board the website lists, and how far down a new score is still announced in Slack. Null restores the default (10 for the main board, 3 otherwise). Presentation only: every row is kept.

post.summary: Collapse one category into another (existing rows and future submissions)
Point another table id at an existing scoreboard
Start a competition — the table board shows only scores set from now on
End a competition — old and competition scores merge back together

get.summary: Slack announcement outbox, plus whether a posting transport is available
get.description: Announcements are composed and stored before they are sent. Foundry holds the workspace Slack credential and posts on the app's behalf: delivery is an authenticated slack.post_message tool call to the Foundry MCP Gateway, never a webhook or a key handed to this app. The target channel is resolved to an approved channel id via slack.channels, which is live authorization state rather than configuration. A rate limit or platform outage leaves a message queued for the next drain; a terminal refusal (channel_not_allowed, validation_error, not_entitled) marks it failed instead of retrying forever.

200.description: Transport status, settings and recent messages

post.summary: Post a test message to the configured channel

get.summary: Raw score rows, newest first, with provenance
get.description: Each row carries map_version, extractor_version and source_slot, plus sightings (how many runs have reported it) and reconfirmed (another map_version has since reported the same row). Any filter may be set to "@none" to match rows stored without that field.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category slug; "main" or "null" for the main board

delete.summary: Retract a bad extraction run in bulk
delete.description: Scoped by provenance — at least one of map_version, extractor_version or source_slot is required, and "@none" matches rows stored before provenance existed. The same table / category / initials filters as the GET narrow it further. Without confirm=true nothing is deleted: the response reports how many rows match, a per-table/category breakdown, how many of them another run has also reported, and a sample. With confirm=true a reason is required; the removed rows are kept on the audit record so the retraction can be restored.

parameters.name: skip_reconfirmed
parameters.description: Keep rows another map_version has also reported since

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Without this the call is a dry run and deletes nothing

200.description: Dry-run counts, or the result of the retraction

400.description: Not scoped by provenance, or confirmed without a reason

get.summary: Extraction runs present in the database
get.description: map_version + extractor_version grouped, with row counts, tables touched and first/last seen.

get.summary: Audit log of bulk retractions

post.summary: Re-insert the rows a retraction removed
